column2: Recite a Sutra
As an observant Buddhist, you often feel great pressure to rule your kingship in line with Dharma perhaps it is time to return to the sayings of Buddha for a bit clarity.
Celebrate Vesak
Whether its called Vesak or Buddha Day, Buddhist celebrate the Birth, Nirvana, and Parinirvana of the Buddha which is usually accompanied by widespread celebration.
Terma Exploration

Faithful Rime followers can embark on an expedition to unearth the "hidden treasures" or Earth-Terma of the earthly realm as part of their efforts to uncover esoterics truths and transmitted across the generations by elder masters of old.
Resolute Peace
This character has read a sutra, which has created a sense of ease and rejuvenation in thier kingship.
Wise Sayings
This character has read a sutra, which has created a clearer sense of understanding of dharma and thier kingship.
Karmic Fury
This character has read a sutra, which has espouses their kingship and thier role as earthly judges of Karma and Dharma.
Tending Gardens
This character has read a sutra for which life is of particular importance and thus they cultivate a garden in accordance to Dharma.
Celebrate Vesak
This Character is celebrating Vesak.
Failed Fast
This character has failed their vow of asceticism.
Building Stupa
This character is building a magnificent Stupa in the name of the Buddha.
Glad Bhikku
This character has donated alms to the local temple and has made wonders for their bhikku.
Donated a prized Earth-Terma
May my vow of asceticism be fruitful...
You feel queezy but you must power through.
Buddhist Opinion
A Tranquil Recollection

As a pious buddhist and ruler, you often wrestle as the Buddha did in tending to the worldly endeavors and the pursuit of Enlightment. Both roles seemingly in opposites you have retired to your room for the night to contemplate. You rest upon a mat and produced a copy of the [Root.Religion.GetScriptureName] and begin sifting through the myraid of sutras and wise teachings of the Buddha and his students for something that may answer your current conundrum. Your hands quiver as the dim glow of the candle drew your eyes to one sutra that seems to be the answer you seek.
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
Perhaps I should rest...
An Auspicious Sutra

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"As you just said, your love was caused by your mind and eyes but if you do not knowwhere your mind and eyes really are, you will never be able to destroy delusion. For instance, when the country is invaded by bandits, the king, before sending his soldiers to destroy them, should first know where they are. That which causes you to transmigrate without interruption, comes from defects in your mind and eyes. Now tell me where your mind and eyes are."...
Fundamentally, everything that comes and goes, that comes into being and ceases to be, is within the true nature of the Matrix of the Thus-Come One, which is the wondrous, everlasting understanding — the unmoving, all-pervading, wondrous suchness of reality.
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, as you reminded of this verse you recall the Buddha's myraid response of the falsehoods of perception which mars the beauty of perfected wisdom and dharma. You peacefully wonder whether as King you have let your world-weary perceptions cloud your judgement...

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"Then the Venerable One said to Ananda, "Tell me, Ananda, whether some god urged you to put this question to the Buddha or whether you asked about his glorious countenance from your own wise observation." Ananda replied to the Buddha, "No god came to prompt me. I asked you about this matter of my own accord."...

You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, Boddhi Ananda on his own will presented before the most auspicous the dilemma of the Compassion of Sentinent Beings. And his excellence laid before Anada the truth of Dhamma and Tathagata... of which you believe may answer at least for the time-being your personal struggle of Kingship. For a compassionate ruler rules true and in accordance to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] by respecting and honoring signs of compassion in their subject and must act to correct those who turn away compassion for the pursuit of proclaiming themselves gods of empty pleasures.

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"Bodhisattvas who practice, the Insight that Brings Us to the Other Shore see no more obstacles in their mind, and because there are no more obstacles in their mind, they can overcome all fear, destroy all wrong perceptions and realize Perfect Nirvana... All Buddhas in the past, present and future by practicing the Insight that Brings Us to the Other Shore are all capable of attaining Authentic and Perfect Enlightenment... Gate, Gate, Paragate, Parasamgate, Bodhi Svaha!"
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, what has gripped you was the feeling of the void of desire, the shaker of truth, fear itself. You recall the six fears as told by the Auspicious One to Anada before in view of the Venerable King of Gesar. By Purging doubt and fear one can touch to the "Heart" of Perfect Wisdom as the Thus-Gone One had in times long gone and to come...

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"Blessed One, I ask this of the Thus-Gone One on behalf of bodhisattvas who dwell on the levels and swiftly bring the level of buddhahood to culmination, who actualize the inconceivable perfection through skillful means, who develop with little hardship the inconceivable skill as a means to bring beings to maturity, and who practice in order to manifest wisdom that will eradicate beings' nonvirtuous qualities and foster their virtuous qualities, serve the family line of the Omniscient One, and lead countless thousands of beings to the level where one is destined for unsurpassed and perfect buddhahood. Blessed One, I ask this on behalf of those who teach the path of awakening to sentient beings and bodhisattvas and who delight in the qualities of buddhahood."
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, you wonder whether what you were lacking was introspection of your own path to buddhahood, you stand renewed in cultivating within yourself the eight noble truths to vanquish the empty pleasures.
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
An Auspicious Sutra

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"Those who always dwell in mindfulness,
Observing measure in the food they eat,
Find that their discomfort grows the less.
Aging gently, life for them is long."

You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, renewed in your vigor to live in accordance to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"But when a person discerns the origination, ending, allure, drawbacks of, and escape from the sense input, he discerns what is higher than all views."

You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, learning a great lesson about overcoming rhetoric so that you may shape the world in better balance and live in accordance to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:\n"Thus, friends, from goods not being distributed to the needy, poverty grew rife, from poverty growing rife stealing increased, from the spread of stealing violence grew apace, from the growth of violence the destruction of life became common, from the frequency of murder lying grew common, from lying growing common, evil speaking grew abundant, from evil speaking growing abundant, adultery grew common, from adultery growing common abusive and idle talk grew common, from abusive and idle talk growing common, covetousness and ill-will grew common, from covetousness and ill-will growing common, false opinions grew common, from false opinions growing common, incest, wanton greed and perverted lust grew common, finally from incest, wanton greed and perverted lust growing common lack of filial and religious piety and lack of regard for the head of the family grew great."\nYou arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, as [Root.GetTitle] you must learn to be a justice ruler and exact due justice upon those that shun away from [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:
"Just as the minter, or an apprentice of his, knows, on holding up a scale, that by so much it has dipped down, by so much it has tilted up. Even so a householder, knowing his income and expenses leads a balanced life, neither extravagant nor miserly, knowing that thus his income will stand in excess of his expenses, but not his expenses in excess of his leads a balanced life."

You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, perhaps it is time for you to be humbled by what you have and to balance your life according to the scales of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] for which you should always be mindful of.
An Auspicious Sutra
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
An Auspicious Sutra

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"He who leads all worldly beings to tread the path of liberation, the teacher of all dharmas- He will bring you well-being."
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, you are comforted to consider the Auspicious Ones great mercy for all sentient beings, perhaps this gentle peace he felt in the pure bless of enlightment can inform your earthly kingship in the eyes of your subjects...

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"The protector who, with thoughts of love for all these beings, sustains them always just as he would his only child- He will bring you well-being."
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, much as it is the fathers duty to protect his child it wise that a ruler must nuture enlightment through his good judgement.

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"The alluring one who defeated all the extremists with the Dharma and brought all assemblies under his influence- He will bring you well-being."
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, as a King you must judge those who seek great excess of pleasures with impunity for they harbor within the gnawing void of desire which will rapture them to the endless cycle of Samsara.

Before you lays a most auspicious sutra, you slowly mouth the words of the sutra before you:

"He whose birth, when this whole earth with all its forests shook and trembled, Brought joy for every living creature..."
You arose from your deep thought and observe your surrounding in a new light, you recall the endless debate with the lamas regarding the Buddha's life purpose born into luxury and break his palace of pleasure by committing strenously to be birth again renewed and apart from the endless cycle of Samsara, as a King perhaps it is time to cultivate the desire to break your limitations as to ascend ten-fold to be one in understanding with the Most Auspicious One and Dhamma...
Return to Courtly Affairs

You awake in the morning with a great weight lifted from you... Your late-night meditation on the Buddha's Word has transformed your doubts to new vigor. You greeted your court with an auspicious welcoming. Stunned by the change of your disposition your court attendants say to you: "My [Root.GetTitle], you seem to be gleaming with a great radiance which we have yet seen!" you say unto them...
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] is compassion!
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] is reason!
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] is glorious!
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] is sublime!
You listen intently...
An Auspicious Time

It is tradition during times of Buddhist celebration for rulers to make large donations of food, money, and clothing to the Sangha. Especially pious rulers will fund the construction of stupas or even temples, assigning large portions of land.
I will donate to the most pious Bhikkhu in the realm...
I will build a magnificent stupa!
This is a time of frugality and asceticism
A Vow to Asceticism

The most pious Buddhists see the Month leading up to Vesak as a time of discipline and asceticism and some may choose to undertake a vegetarian fast in order to accrue merit and refrain from sensual pleasures, instead focusing on self-discipline and denial.
I shall consider a fast...
I shall not harm living conscience...
I shall consider a different offering...

You are nearing the end of Fast as your health begins to waver, is your resolve strong enough? You contemplate to yourself has you made enough dedication as The Buddha had to achieve Enlightment? You contemplate quitting or sticking true and feeling as the Buddha did as he sat under the Bodhi Tree.
This is too hard...
I must pull through...
The Fasting Period has ended whether you partook or not in this ritual you feel invigorated as you prepare your realm to put on a grand display of majesty before the realm.
Let us enjoy the occasion.
Preparations for the Parade

On Vesak, the ruler frequently funds a parade on the day of Vesak. Elephants, dancers, musicians, and acrobats march through the streets behind a massive shrine of the Buddha atop the royal elephant all in celebration of that Buddha.

On Buddha Day, the ruler frequently funds a grand parade during Buddha Day. The stately musicians and lion dancers march through the streets and along the rivers with the onlookers beholding a massive shrine of the Buddha atop an ornate float as the sounds of gongs announce the Buddhas Birth in this existence.
I shall fund a massive parade.
I shall fund a worthy parade.
A Day to Remember...

The Day of Vesak has arrived. It was today, over three thousand years ago, that the Buddha Sakkamuni was born. On his birth the devas descended unto the world to pay homage to the future Buddha and the Sage Asita predicted that he would reject the path of the monarch and become the Buddha of this age. Fearing this, his father walled him up with all the pleasures of the world, but the Buddha did indeed leave and became enlightened under the Bodhi Tree exactly 35 years later, for the next 35 years, he lived in Nibbana before finally passing from this and all other world spheres in his Parinibba. It is for this reason we celebrate.
Thus I have heard
A Grand Display

A massive elephant walks down the main thoroughfare, followed by a small legion of acrobats and dancers while musicians play devotional songs. The mood is raucous, perhaps too much for such an occasion say some of the more conservative monks, but the people are overjoyed by the splendor. Regardless of the appropriateness of the mood, it is clear that people are remembering the Buddha on this day.

As the procession walks down the main thoroughfare, a fierce display of lion dancers move between the beating percussions as musicians recite devotional songs. The mood is raucous, perhaps too much for such an occasion say some of the more conservative monks, but the people are overjoyed by the splendor. Regardless of the appropriateness of the mood, it is clear that people are remembering the Buddha on this day.

The royal elephant, decorated in paints and clad in the finest silks, marches down the streets bearing a shrine with a gold Buddha inside for all to see. Behind him acrobats and dancers move through the streets elegantly, their costumes twisting and billowing as they move. Behind them fire-eaters and jugglers amaze the crowd with their skills. A sweet smell of incense comes from the Bhikkhus who bear yet another shrine while they chant suttas and charms in time with a bell. The onlookers pay respect as the Bhikkhus pass, some bowing and others kneeling further while chanting along. The spectacle is immense, yet respectful, and the people are invigorated with the love of the Dhamma.

The float, decorated in the finest crimson paint and clad in the finest silks, sits a lacquer shrine for which the gleaming gold Buddha inside beckons for all to see. Behind him a myriad of dragon and lion dancers move through the streets gracefully, their display twisting and billowing to the racauous percussions. On the float dedicated monks of the pagoda are seen washing the statue of the Buddha before placing delicate lotus buds before his feet. The Display of which caused some onlookers to weep in reverence. A sweet smell of incense comes from the Bhikkhus who bear yet another shrine while they chant suttas and charms in time with a bell. The onlookers pay respect as the Bhikkhus pass, some bowing and others kneeling further while chanting along. The spectacle is immense, yet respectful, and the people are invigorated with the love of the Dhamma.
A Wise Man...

As the initial festivities come to a close, the people gather at temples to listen to the Bhikkhus who chant Suttas for the merit of all listening. A storyteller-Bhikkhu begins to narrate a Jataka on the edge of the temple for the amusement of all, embellishing and gesticulating to enhance the story.
Perhaps this story I have yet heard...
I've heard this many times...
Silanisama Jataka

As you move closer, the Bhikkhu begins to narrate the Silanisama Jataka, The Tale of the Good Friend. "Eons ago, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, there was a pious lay disciple who embarked on a journey with his wealthy friend," he begins. As he narrates the story he embellishes it, adding jokes and quips to the performance and putting on voices for the barber before reaching their ship sinking and them being marooned."It was at that time that the Barber killed a fowl and offered some to the layman who said ‘all I need is the triple gem’ and began to meditate...

As he did so a great King of Nagas appeared before them," he raises his arms and puffs himself up in mock imitation of the spirit. He narrates how the Naga transformed himself into a ship and how a Sea Spirit was captain, but refused the rich man entry as he was not a follower of the path, to which the disciple replied "the fruits of my practice, I give them all to him." The Sea Spirit nodded and took them both home. "Keep company of the wise and pious, that is the teaching of the Buddha," finishes the story-teller.
Vessantara Jataka

As you approach, you hear the Bhikkhu begin the Vessantara Jataka, the Tale of Prince Vessantara. "Eons ago, during the reign of Sivi in Jetuttara in the kingdom of Sivi, the Buddha Vipassi arose in the world.  During this time, a there was born a girl called Phusati…" He narrated the death and fortunate rebirth of Phusati, her marriage to the prince of Sivi, and the birth of her son, Vessantara, a past incarnation of the Buddha.  The crowd begins to cheer at the mention of Vessantara. The Bhikkhu regales the crowd with tales of Vessantara’s generosity and makes jokes along the way, using voices and gestures with much aplomb.

He then reaches the Boddhisatta’s marriage and children, his deeds as prince, and then, to the crowd’s horror and anticipation, his exile. He delights the crowd with his characters as Vessantara gives away his remaining possessions, children, and finally his wife, then the crowd cheers as the Devas spirit them away to the heavens before finally they are triumphantly reunited upon Vessantara’s return to the kingdom and how he reigned for many years before finally taking his penultimate birth in Tushita Heaven. "Though gifts drove him into exile, the merit he acquired was by far the greater gift, this is the teaching of the Buddha."
Vidurapandita Jataka

As you make you way to the Bhikkhu, he begins the Vidurapandita Jataka, the Tale of the Wise Sage. "Many Ages ago, when King Dhanañjaya was reigning in Kuru, he had a wise minister by the name of Vidurapandita…" With great skill and comic sensibility, he narrates the wit of Vidurapandita before telling of the debate of the Garuda King, the Deva king, the Naga King and King Dhanañjaya over who was most virtuous, how the Garuda was restrained, the Deva chaste, the Naga gentle, and Dhanañjaya austere. Then how Vidurapandita was summoned and judged their virtues equal. The tale then took a turn for the dramatic as the Queen of the Nagas desired to hear from Vidurapandita, but knowing her husband was too mild to request he be brought before him, feigned illness saying "The only cure is the heart of Vidurapandita." Distressed, the Naga king sent his daughter to find a way to receive it.

The Bhikkhu dropped into a low tone, almost whispering, as he got to the part where the Naga princess plotted with the Yakkha Prince on how they would steal away Vidurapandita in a game of dice and how finally the Yakkha prince received him. Then, just before the Yakkha prince killed him, Vidurapandita recognized that the heart of a sage was his wisdom and that the Naga queen only wanted him to preach! The crowd laughed at the revelation and cheered as he returned to Dhanañjaya. "Not just in his life as the Buddha, but also in previous lives did he show his mastery of wit, this is the teaching of the Buddha."
Evam me Suttam!
A Resolute End...

As dusk falls over the city, a thousand lamps of every color and shape are lit, some displayed in such a way as to make images in honor of the Buddha. The festivities continue long into the night under the light of the lamps and the full moon.  You see people dancing and singing, monks chanting and meditating, sages and rishis preaching, and yet others resting.  As you finally drift off to sleep, you contemplate your own austerities.

As dusk falls over the city, a thousand lamps of every color and shape are lit, some displayed in such a way as to make images in honor of the Buddha. The festivities continue long into the night under the light of the lamps and the full moon.  You see people dancing and singing, monks chanting and meditating, sages and rishis preaching, and yet others resting.  As you finally drift off to sleep, you think back on the Buddha and his deeds, contemplating the power of virtue.
I have accrued enough merits...
...But I could yet accrue more
It was a good day...
The Earthly Realm

It is said that all over the Earthly Realm powerful tantric artifacts known as Earth-Terma lay in wait and according to tradition contain "hidden treasures" of understanding that many of the Rime Faith strive to find. These artifacts come in many forms: ritual objects, sacred texts and simply magical objects left behind by those that walk before us. While the event has sundered the world from the old connections some hold out hope that some of these relics hold those secrets within...\n\nAcquiring such Earth-Terma will not only bring me great renown and prestige, it is the sacred duty of all adherences of the Rime Movement.
Hmmm, where will I find well-preserved terma?

You check the maps, and have located several potential expedition sites in the province of [From.GetName]. The people of [From.GetName] follow the [From.Religion.GetName] faith, and are culturally [From.Culture.GetName].\n\nProvinces populated by the ignorant are more likely to contain items of spiritual significance, since they do not have the traditions of terma.
That will be my destination.
That province is unacceptable.
Before leaving on your Terma Expedition to [From.GetName], it would be wise to make preparations.
Set out with your men.
Consult the masters for good terma locations.
Assemble a battle-hardened warband to accompany you.
Send envoys ahead to smooth your travels.
Unfriendly Locals

You arrive in [From.GetName], and many of the local residents are distrustful or outright hostile towards you and your men. You notice them amuleting you surreptitiously and talking amongst themselves, and have a difficult time finding a place to rest.
Ignore them.
We're well armed, they won't risk attacking us.
My envoys have arranged for reliquary passage.
Try to keep a low profile.

Other Terma Specialists from a nearby realm are attempting to retrieve the Earth-Terma from your lands in [Root.GetName]. Their presence seems to be drawing the ire of the local [Root.Religion.GetName] population, who are preparing for a confrontation with them.
Let the locals drive them away.
We must avoid bloodshed.

Mixed among the local residents in [From.GetName], you see the occasional soldier wearing the colors of [From.Holder.GetTitledFirstName]. Fortunately, the soldiers seem to be ensuring that order is maintained and the locals allow you to pass without conflict.
Hostile Locals

Your continued presence in [From.GetName] has drawn the ire of the local peasantry, and you are now confronted by a disorganized mob of angry villagers. They may not be well armed, and they're certainly not well trained...\n\n...but there are a lot of them.
We should turn back.
Your Terma Expedition is over.
Your Terma Expedition continues.
We can fight our way through!
They'll back down from a vulgar display of power!
Peasants like silver, right?
Driven from [From.From.GetName]
Hordes of angry local villagers have driven you from their lands, ending your Terma Expedition. If it makes you feel better, tell yourself you left to avoid shedding THEIR blood.
Competing Terma Specialist
During your expedition to [From.GetName], you encounter an agent of an unknown lord who shares your faith. He appears to be scouting new terma sites for his master, in direct competition with you!
May the best Terma Specialist win!
Direct him to a promising site nearby.
Make him disappear.
Collapse!

You hoped the wooden reinforcement beams would be enough, but one of them slipped. The centuries have not been kind to the crumbling stone and supports, and the whole unstable mess is coming down around you!
Run for it!
I won't let debris stand in my way!
I planned for this risk.
Recent Terma
This character has recently gone on a Terma Expedition.
Preparing Expedition
This character is preparing to go on a Terma Expedition.
Terma in [From.GetName]
Your expedition has turned up very little valuable terma. You have explored many ruined buildings, and everywhere you look you find the ruins picked clean.
Disappointing.
Someone has been here before me...
There is another site nearby we could check.

Your expedition has turned up a few items of useful terma. In the ruined buildings and tunnels you have uncovered several artifacts, though you have not yet found the kind of major prize you were hoping for.
At least I found something.
Hawk these trinkets, I know of another site.

Your men have discovered a large metal box beneath the ruins of a long-forgotten structure in [From.GetName]. The strongbox is corroded but still intact. Who knows what mystical relics of Old are sealed within it?
I'll know soon, crack it open!
Have your tinker open it carefully.
Terma

You have found conch shells, but none of them are especially unblemished by the ruins around it. There are objects that may have once been used for to make nice jewelry and serve as offerings, but it's hard to tell with the fragments that remain. They might be worth a few gold pieces to the right buyer.

Your men have discovered a cache of corroded tokens from an old box. Their tokens were inexplicably made out of base metals rather than gold or silver, dramatically reducing their value as ritualistic artifacts but perhaps they could be a nice gift for the local market-goer.

You have discovered a long-hidden supply of Old World herbs. Unlike objects of precious stones and metal, well aired herbs can still be useful in rituals. You need but wipe off the centuries and you'll have fine collection of herbs to burn as incense with a mysterious aura of days long gone.

Amongst the ruins you stumble before a lonesome shadow just beyond your perception, you find a fabulously preserved piece of a statues of Bodhisattvas and furious Mahakala. Though blemished by sands of time, the beautiful object itself does not seem to have rusted. It is about five feet tall, with an enlightened fearsome pose befitting their rank. It is sturdy and seemingly "warm" by grace itself.\n\nThis will be a great addition to your great hall, or part of a shrine.

Your men carefully pull apart the ancient box, and succeed in prying the door off after a few hours. Whether it was the rough handling of the box, the ravages of time and moisture, or simple bad luck, you find nothing of value within.
Treasures!

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a variety of precious jewels, glittering with gold, silver, and precious stones. The craftsmanship is finer and more intricate than what modern goldsmiths can produce.
Ancient Folios

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: several old folios bound with crumbling dark leather and stacks of wooden and stone tablets etched with ancient sutras. It's amazing how well the box has preserved its contents, the seal must have been perfect. The folios are filled with line after line of ancient sayings though hard to read.\n\nPerhaps with a bit more examination these texts could be illuminating to your court.
Paintings?

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a collection of dozens of tiny paintings, discolored with age but extremely detailed. The paintings depict events both mythological and seemingly historical. How these paintings were produced is a mystery to you, as the canvas is very thin and there are no visible brush strokes.\n\nThe cracked and crumbling condition of the paintings makes you think they are unlikely to last long after being removed from the sealed reliquary.

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a collection of small ornate bells meant to be held. Each bell is exquisitely crafted you happily give it a little ring and to your surprise it still works, playing a soft melody that has probably not been played for centuries at the very least.\n\nThis will be a hit among the court but especially in the primacy of the temple masters.
Powerful!

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a small wood-bound drum with various bits of sinews and brittle wood attached to it. You've heard that this is a damaru, a tool instrumental in many pieces of music but this particular damaru seem of an exceptional quality that you have never seen before.\n\nThough the reliquary has preserved it well, you will have to handle it gently and be unable to fix it if it breaks.

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a well preserved khata its silk cotton and gold embroidery surprisingly intact despite its apparent age. Expert weaves display prayers and scenes from across the Buddha's life, each labeled with a unique signature of this ancient weaver.\n\nAside from its religious significance it could be hung up if handled with exceptional care and restoration to make it sparkle...

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a well preserved piece of Vajra Dorje or "Thunderbolt". Representing the industriability of Diamond and the furious power of Lightning, it craft is exceptional and engraved with magical runes.\n\nFor its beauty one must be gentle in how to use and maintain it...

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a golden, palm-sized square mirror reflecting the face of the buddha, attached to an intricate chain of precious stones. When you clean the dust off it you seen a protection rune scrawled across the edges from ancient tantric masters, and you realize that the artifact is an ancient protection amulet.\n\nIt would be a stylish accessory for any lord, but it would be even more useful if you could understand its workings and avoid attracting unwanted spirits.

The reliquary door finally opens, and you can see the contents: a pair of cymbals intricately designed and smooth like polished glass. This instrument forms one of the sacred instruments during rituals back at home.
Terma Expedition ends

Not all Terma Expeditions end in success. Sometimes the recovered artifacts are badly damaged, sometimes they are worthless, sometimes there isn't anything to terma because the area has been picked clean, and sometimes dangerous circumstances interrupt the expedition.\n\nThis is one of those times.
Until next time.

You have returned from your Terma Expedition with baubles and artifacts from the ancient ruins. Although you did not find an Earth Terma truly worthy of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]'s favor, at least you didn't return empty handed.
I'll keep the terma for myself.
